messages:
alex_k: Heads up — I switched my 401(k) contribution from Roth to pre-tax on the self-service portal yesterday afternoon (after payroll cutoff?). Does that mean I'll be deducted twice for this pay period or will the change apply next cycle? I didn't see confirmation email. cc @sam_benefits

sam_benefits: Hey @alex_k — can you share the timestamp of the change? Usually changes made after payroll cutoff apply next cycle, but if the vendor accepted a file we may need to manually adjust. No double deduction in most cases, but there are exceptions with vendor migrations.

alex_k: Change recorded at 2026-03-22 16:38 PT in the portal. Portal showed "success" but no email.

sam_benefits: Thanks. We're migrating recordkeeping to BrightPath next week which complicates mid-pay changes. I'll check with payroll. @payroll-bot do you see any transactions for alex_k in current payroll feed for 03/26 run? 

payroll-bot: payroll-bot: Ran feed for 03/26 at 03/26 04:00 UTC. No manual adjustments flagged. Found a deduction record for alex_k: 401k_pre_tax $200 scheduled. No Roth entry for this pay period.

lina_peopleops: FYI — if a double deduction does happen, payroll can issue a net-pay correction (refund) the next business day but we prefer vendor-level reversal so reporting matches. Sam, do we have the BrightPath cutover window documented? 

sam_benefits: Cutover is 03/28 00:00 UTC. Any changes submitted before 03/28 00:00 UTC should be in the legacy vendor file; after that they'll go to BrightPath. Since alex changed on 03/22, should be in legacy. But sometimes the portal resubmits to the new vendor when it syncs — edge case.

kevin_dev: I had similar thing last quarter when vendor switch caused a duplicate deduction for one person. Payroll fixed it with a BEN-ADJ refund and we updated HRIS. @sam_benefits do you want me to paste the example CSV we used? 

sam_benefits: Yes please — that helps payroll. Kevin, paste the minimal format we used.

kevin_dev: ```
employee_id, pay_date, adjustment_code, amount, reason
E12345,2026-03-26,BEN-ADJ,-200,duplicate 401k pre-tax deduction
```

payroll-bot: payroll-bot: If a duplicate is discovered, submit the adjustment CSV to payroll-inbox@redwood.com with subject "BEN-ADJ — <pay_period> — <employee_ids>". Payroll will apply in next payroll cycle; for urgent refunds request payroll@redwood.com with "URGENT REFUND". Cutoff for manual adjustments for 03/26 run was 03/25 11:59 PT.

tanya_hsa: Quick question while we're on benefits — if I change 401(k) from Roth to pre-tax, does that affect my HSA eligibility for 2026? I hit the HSA limit and want to make sure tax status change doesn't break anything.

sam_benefits: Changing 401(k) type doesn't affect HSA eligibility. HSA eligibility is about HDHP enrollment and not being on Medicare/claimed as dependent. Contribution limits for 2026: $3,900 individual / $7,750 family, plus $1,000 catch-up if 55+. (See internal benefits doc: https://intranet.redwood.com/benefits/2026-hsa-limits)

tanya_hsa: Awesome, thanks.

sam_benefits: Action items: @alex_k — please forward any portal success email or screenshot. We'll monitor payroll feed; if duplicate appears, payroll will apply BEN-ADJ refund. I'll open a small support ticket with BrightPath to confirm no double-submission. ETA 1 business day.

alex_k: Screenshot attached in DM to @sam_benefits. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sam_benefits: Got it — closing loop once payroll confirms or issues adjustment."
